bugClass.title: Stale tracker endpoint drops the full snapshot
bugClass.cause: A client or transport is hard-coded to an older tracker read endpoint and expects its response to be the collection itself. After the tracker migrates that data to a fixed status endpoint with a nested array, the request fails or response parsing yields no items, and the client discards the entire snapshot instead of reading the new shape.
bugClass.criteria: Classify another site when a runtime client or transport reads tracker state through a legacy endpoint or parses its response as the collection, and an endpoint or response-shape change can therefore make a whole snapshot disappear. The cause qualifies whether the stale endpoint causes request failure or the client fails to extract a collection nested in a status response. Do not classify merely because code references a tracker endpoint if it tolerates migration or falls back to the fixed status response and its machines array.

candidates.evidence: Lines 14–20 configure test fixture URLs for legacy `/items`, `/runs`, and `/machines` endpoints, but the excerpt describes a test double and does not show the runtime reader or snapshot discard behavior. Trigger and any fallback are not established here.

Lines 11–26 define synthetic test routes for legacy endpoints and `/status`; the excerpt does not show how the runtime client chooses or parses these responses, or whether it discards the snapshot after a migration.

Lines 51–56 document machine records as coming from `/machines` or `/status.machines`, which indicates shape awareness, but the excerpt does not establish the client's request path, extraction behavior, or fallback.

Lines 178–191 test acceptance of the `/items` list response and assert 11 items, but this is repository test code, not the runtime tracker reader; it does not establish whole-snapshot loss on endpoint or shape change.
Lines 58–66 test the local API's `/items?status=all&limit=-1` response, not a runtime tracker-state client. No endpoint migration failure or full-snapshot discard mechanism is shown.

Lines 119–124 exercise the local `/items` API and verify an item list response after polling. The excerpt does not show a tracker client reading legacy state or dropping a snapshot after an endpoint or response-shape change.
